what_was_done: Pinned the two unpinned rules of the allow-list with tests; the code was already right and is unchanged for this finding. (1) A single-quoted string holds no character below U+0020 and no U+007F: REFUSED_CALLS in test_caller.py gains six calls whose single-quoted argument holds, in turn, a tab, a newline, a carriage return, a NUL, an escape character and DEL ('vsdd survey a\tb' and friends), so test_allow_list_refuses_every_excluded_character and test_allow_list_regex_refuses_the_tables_on_its_own cover the rule; and the property test's between-quotes position now draws from an alphabet that holds every control character below U+0020 and DEL besides the excluded characters and the single quote. The between-quotes construction anchors the span with a plain x ('vsdd survey --flag value 'x<junk>''), so a widened span class cannot swallow the junk and close the argument cleanly: restoring _QUOTED = r"'[^']*'" now fails three tests (the refusal table, the regex-alone table and test_property_junk_from_excluded_characters_never_approves, caught in 51 of its 200 draws; the old doubled-quote construction caught none), and letting only the tab in fails two. (2) A quoted string may follow a bare word only when that word ends with '=': REFUSED_CALLS gains 'vsdd survey a\'b'', a bare letter directly followed by a quoted string; loosening the prefix to (?:(?!=)[_SAFE_]*)? in caller.py fails the refusal table and the regex-alone table. Both new-table facts also travel with the property test, which asserts every drawing is refused while caller._CALL_TEXT_RE and the parser both hold. Mutation proofs ran in a scratch copy of next/ built from the pre-fix tree; each mutation was restored byte-identically afterwards.
where: next/tests/hooks/test_caller.py (REFUSED_CALLS: six control-character quoted spans and vsdd survey a'b'; test_property_junk_from_excluded_characters_never_approves: the between-quotes alphabet and anchor)

what_was_done: The program alternative of _CALL_TEXT_RE in caller.py now begins the path with a letter, a digit, '_', '.' or '/' — (?:vsdd|[A-Za-z0-9_./][A-Za-z0-9_@%+:,./-]*/vsdd) — so a first word beginning with '%' (a job spec in bash 3.2, bash 5.3, macOS /bin/sh and zsh, which run the fg builtin instead of the path) and a path beginning with '-' or '+' (the /bin/sh interpreter of a #!/bin/sh script reads the word as options, so the call is approved and can never work) are refused. The code comment in caller.py states the rule and the reason, and the grammar passage of rewrite/spec/topics/caller-identity.md now says the path begins with a letter, digit, '_', '.' or '/', with the reason. REFUSED_CALLS gains '%/vsdd survey', '%1/vsdd x', '-x/vsdd survey' and '+/vsdd survey'; the runner test test_refused_bypass_forms_pass_unmarked_through_the_runner sends all four through the gate as an agent. Proof: with the pre-fix caller.py restored (scratch copy), the three tests fail — the refusal table, the regex-alone table and the runner test, which records the marker, permissionDecision 'allow' and updatedInput that '%/vsdd survey' drew from the pre-fix code. A canary sweep over 318 grammar-accepted texts (program forms vsdd, ./vsdd, sub/vsdd, 1/vsdd, _x/vsdd, .x/vsdd, x.y/vsdd; bare words; single-quoted spans holding spaces, non-ASCII and shell metacharacters; name='value' forms; space/tab padding) ran under /bin/sh, /bin/bash 3.2, bash 5.3, /bin/dash and /bin/zsh: each text ran the vsdd canary exactly once and no decoy ever ran, with a per-shell negative control proving the harness records hidden runs.
where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/hooks/caller.py (_CALL_TEXT_RE program alternative, _QUOTED area comments); rewrite/spec/topics/caller-identity.md (grammar passage, the program bullet); next/tests/hooks/test_caller.py (REFUSED_CALLS, test_refused_bypass_forms_pass_unmarked_through_the_runner)
